verdict: READY TO MERGE - 18 of 18 findings resolved, 0 bubbled
strengths: test_utf8_stdin_survives_a_legacy_console_codepage runs the real script in a subprocess with PYTHONIOENCODING=cp1252 for both --block and --all. Without the stdin reconfigure, the arrow decodes to mojibake and the JSON assertion fails, so the test can fail on Linux CI too.
TestMessageAll.test_a_bad_section_exits_1_and_writes_nothing puts a valid block before the bad one and compares the skeleton bytes, which pins that set_messages applies all sections or none.
parse_block_messages gets a table of each malformed-input class (no header, stray lead text, duplicate, blank section), and each case matches its own error text.

The double-quote tests cover the edge cases: a quote inside backticks is still flagged, single quotes and backticks pass, the message line number is reported, and txt_to_commit_dict skips only the bad TXT while still writing the good sibling .ps1.
The capture-once test wraps the real capture_branch with a counting spy, so the diff output stays real and the test is not a mock chain.
run_diff_blocks resolves every requested block (_block_paths) before the git capture, so an unknown block fails fast without paying for a capture.
set_messages chains immutable set_message copies and writes once, so an unknown block in message --all leaves the skeleton untouched, as the docstring promises.
One quote rule (_commit_quote_problems) feeds both build validation and the .ps1 driver path, so the two cannot drift apart.
argparse mutually exclusive required groups enforce --block vs --all for both subcommands, and dict.fromkeys dedupes repeated --block values in order.
block_header is the one source for the ##### block N ##### line in both diff output and message --all input.

The double-quote rule is stated once in commit_format.md with the real failure mode (the rest of the message reaching git as pathspecs) and matches `_commit_quote_problems` in commit_txt.py exactly, including that backticks do not exempt a quote.

The `message --all` docs (header line format, block left out keeps its message, unknown or empty block writes nothing) agree with `parse_block_messages` and `set_messages` in branch_commit_msg.py, and the usage synopsis in the script docstring matches the argparse groups.

branch-commit-msg and c-msg build steps now route message fixes back through `message` rather than JSON edits, and the Common Mistakes tables gained rows naming the per-block round trips the PR removes.
run_diff_blocks captures once per call and run_diff stays a thin wrapper with byte-identical one-block output, pinned by a test.
message --all is all-or-nothing: parsing and set_messages raise before write_skeleton, and a test proves the skeleton is unchanged on a bad section.
The cp1252 stdin test runs the real script in a subprocess with PYTHONIOENCODING=cp1252, so it fails on any OS without the fix.
Skill contract tests parse the skill command lines with the real parser, so the --all and repeated --block forms cannot drift.
The quote ban is enforced at build and at driver generation, with a line number in each problem.

important.name: Quote ban breaks carried messages that amend keeps byte for byte
important.summary: message_problems rejects a double quote in every block (commit_txt.py line 276) and txt_to_commit_dict skips any TXT holding one (lines 159-162). Drafts from before 0.34.0 carry quoted messages forward, so build fails on blocks the change never named. amend Step 2 (lines 69-71) says every other message stays byte for byte, and c-msg skips a carried message that still matches (lines 47-49), so neither skill allows the only fix. No doc warns that old drafts now fail build and .ps1 generation.
fix: amend and c-msg Step 2: a build `double quote` problem forces a rewrite of that block limited to swapping the quotes for backticks or single quotes.
Have capture print a `note:` per carried block holding a double quote.

important.name: amend-commit-msg Step 5 still says 'fix the JSON' after the skill banned editing the skeleton
important.summary:
The PR moved message writing in this skill to `message --all` and the sibling skills' build steps were reworded ('Fix the message with `message` (Step 3)' in branch-commit-msg:164, 'set the message again (Step 2)' in c-msg:76), but amend-commit-msg Step 5 still ends with 'fix the JSON and rerun'. The skill's Quiet run rule (line 36) and Common Mistakes row (line 144) forbid Edit/Write on the skeleton, so the build-failure path points the agent at the one action the skill prohibits, and the Edit diff it produces is the round trip this PR is removing. Line 98 ('move the bullet by hand') has the same gap: by hand now means rewriting both messages with `message --all`.

Also (overall): The PR routes every message write through `message` and bans Edit on the skeleton (amend SKILL.md line 36, branch-commit-msg Step 4, c-msg Step 3). amend-commit-msg Step 5 still says `fix the JSON and rerun`, and agents/messenger.md line 87 says `fix the JSON as the skill says`, steering back to the Edit round trip this PR removes. The new no-Fix-the-JSON contract test covers only branch-commit-msg.
fix: Replace 'fix the JSON and rerun' at line 135 with 'fix it with `message` (Step 4) or `move` (Step 3) and rerun', and at line 98 replace 'move the bullet by hand' with 'rewrite both blocks' messages in the Step 4 `message --all` call'.

amend SKILL.md line 135: say fix the message with `message` (Step 4) or the grouping with `move` (Step 3). messenger.md line 87: say fix it as the skill says. Add the not-in assertion to test_amend_commit_msg_skill_contract.py.

important.name: branch-commit-msg Step 3 diffs every block while telling the agent to skip carried and canned ones
important.summary:
Step 3 opens with 'For each block whose message is empty (or whose carried message no longer matches its diff), read what changed. Skip a block with a canned message', then prescribes `diff "<skeleton>" --all`. In `_cmd_diff` (plugins/harness/scripts/branch_commit_msg.py:753) `--all` expands to every key in the skeleton, so a default (non-fresh) capture with mostly carried messages, plus the canned TODO/review-artifact block, prints up to BLOCK_BUDGET (300 lines) per block for blocks the step says to skip. Repeated `--block` already shares one capture (`run_diff_blocks` captures once for any block list), so `--all` buys no round trip over naming the blocks that need a message; it only adds output. For a PR whose goal is cutting the run's cost, the default command contradicts the sentence above it.

Also (overall): branch-commit-msg Step 3 (lines 101-105) says skip a canned block, then prescribes `diff --all`, and _cmd_diff (branch_commit_msg.py line 753) selects every block, each with its own 300-line budget. On large branches the saved round trips come back as context tokens.
fix: Make the fenced command `diff "<skeleton>" --block <key> [--block <key> ...]` naming only the blocks with an empty or stale message, keep `--all` as the case where every block needs a message (a `--fresh` capture), and update the pin at tests/skills/test_branch_commit_msg_skill_contract.py:97 to match.

Keep `--all` but add one sentence after the command: when the skeleton carries messages or holds a canned block, name only the blocks to write with repeated `--block` instead; one call still covers them all.
Prescribe `--block` for the non-canned blocks when any block is canned.
Or have `--all` print a one-line skipped marker for a canned block.

important.name: run_diff equality assertion is tautological
important.summary:
test_one_block_matches_run_diff_without_a_header asserts run_diff_blocks(clone, payload, [2]) == run_diff(clone, payload, 2), but at the head run_diff (branch_commit_msg.py:412-414) is a one-line delegate to run_diff_blocks(repo, payload, [block]). The first assertion compares a function with itself and cannot fail. Only the second line (no `#####` in the output) carries the contract, so the single-block output format has no independent pin.

Also (tests): TestDiffBlocks says `one capture for the whole call`, and test_the_branch_is_captured_once_for_every_block counts only capture_branch. _block_diff (branch_commit_msg.py:386) calls untracked_paths(repo), which runs `git ls-files --others`, once per block, and capture_stats calls it once more. A diff --all over N blocks therefore runs N+1 untracked listings. That per-block git cost is what this performance PR targets, and the test cannot see it.
fix: Replace the equality with an independent expectation of the single-block form: out = script.run_diff_blocks(clone, payload, [2]); assert out.startswith(`=== docs/new.md`) and that `#####` is not in out.
Or compare against the text _block_diff produces for block 2, built from its own capture, so the test checks the no-header branch rather than the delegate.

Compute the untracked set once in run_diff_blocks and pass it to _block_diff. Then extend the spy test to also wrap untracked_paths, both on the script module and on harness_lib.branch_capture, and assert it is called a fixed number of times regardless of block count.
If per-block listing is intended, narrow the class docstring to `one capture_branch call` so it does not claim more than the test checks.

important.name: amend-commit-msg build step still says fix the JSON, and no contract test catches it
important.summary: The PR moves every message write onto the `message` command and pins that route for branch-commit-msg (test_a_build_problem_is_fixed_through_the_message_command asserts `Fix the JSON` is gone from Step 4) and for c-msg (`edit the JSON` absent). The amend contract gets no matching pin, and amend-commit-msg/SKILL.md:135 Step 5 still reads `fix the JSON and rerun` after a build problem. That contradicts the skill rule `never use Edit or Write on the skeleton`, and it is the path most likely to send the session back to hand-editing the skeleton, which this PR set out to remove. test_skill_writes_messages_through_the_script_and_stays_quiet only checks that the Step 4 message command exists.
fix: Add to test_amend_commit_msg_skill_contract.py a Step 5 slice assertion like the branch-commit-msg one: the body between `## Step 5` and `## Common Mistakes` does not contain `fix the json` (compared in lower case) and does name the `message` command as the fix route. Then reword amend-commit-msg/SKILL.md:135 to `fix the message with message (Step 4) and rerun` so the new test passes.

minor.name: Multi-block diff still lists untracked files once per block
minor.summary: run_diff_blocks says the branch is captured once per call, but _block_diff calls untracked_paths(repo) (a `git ls-files --others` subprocess) for every block, on top of the calls inside capture_branch and capture_stats. `diff --all` over N blocks spawns N+2 identical listings, which works against the point of this performance PR.
fix: Compute `untracked = set(untracked_paths(repo))` once in run_diff_blocks and pass it to _block_diff as a parameter in place of the per-block call.
Derive the untracked set from the captures already taken (the entries merge_capture built from the untracked listing) and pass it to _block_diff.

minor.name: stdin decoded as utf-8, not utf-8-sig, so a BOM breaks message --all
minor.summary: main reconfigures stdin to plain utf-8. A pipe from Windows PowerShell with a UTF-8 $OutputEncoding can start with U+FEFF, and str.strip() does not remove U+FEFF. With --all the first header line then fails _BLOCK_HEADER.fullmatch and the run exits with 'text before the first ##### block N ##### line'. With --block the BOM is stored at the start of the subject, so build later reports a subject-rule error that is hard to trace.
fix: Reconfigure stdin with encoding='utf-8-sig' (stdout stays 'utf-8'), so a leading BOM is dropped on read.
Strip a leading '﻿' from `text` in _cmd_message before parsing or setting.

minor.name: Quote ban also blocks the --json dump, which never reaches git
minor.summary:
_load_or_report applies quote_problems to every load, so `txt_to_commit_dict.py <branch> --json` on a TXT with a double quote prints `null` and exits 1. According to _commit_quote_problems, the ban exists because the PowerShell commit driver passes the message to `git commit -m`. JSON output builds no driver, so inspecting a legacy TXT is refused for a reason that does not apply to it.

Also (overall): _load_or_report (lines 159-162) skips a TXT that parses but holds a double quote, for both .ps1 and --json. The module docstring (lines 15-18) names only validation failures, and --json writes no driver, so the skip hides a document from inspection for a rule that only the PowerShell driver needs.
fix: Run quote_problems only on the .ps1 path (in main, before write_ps1), and keep _load_or_report limited to parse validation.
Keep the check for both modes, but state in the module docstring (lines 15-18) that a double quote in a message skips the file in --json mode too.
State the skip in the module docstring.
Apply quote_problems only on the .ps1 path in main().

fix: amend-commit-msg:77: append '(one block prints without the header line)'; branch-commit-msg:108-109: move that parenthetical so it covers `--all` on a one-block skeleton too, e.g. 'A single block, named or the only one, prints without the header line.'

minor.name: Negative prose pins are case-sensitive
